title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 77
paragraphs: When they appeared at the gates, things happened nearly as Darius had supposed. The guards, showing respect for men who were the chief among the Persians, and not suspecting anything of what was afoot, allowed them to pass inside under divine guidance, and no one asked them any question. When they had passed into the court, they met the eunuchs who carried messages in to the king. These inquired of them why they had come, and at the same time threatened the gate-keepers with punishment for having let them pass, and tried to stop the seven when they attempted to go further. Then the seven gave the word to one another, drew their daggers, and stabbed on the spot the men who tried to stop them; and they themselves ran on towards the men's chamber.
